title: Is Organic Food a scam?
summary: Commentator's review finding organic uses natural pesticides that are not always safer, label tiers allow non-organic content, yields are lower and land use higher, environmental results are mixed, nutrition is similar apart from antioxidants, and residues are lower.

assertions.quote: Most people think it means no pesticides, but that's absolutely not true. Organic farmers can and do use pesticides.
They just have to be derived from natural sources.
some of those natural pesticides can be more toxic than synthetic ones
If a label says organic in the US, it has to consist of at least 95% organic ingredients.

verdicts.note: 7 CFR 205.301 requires at least 95 percent organic content, excluding water and salt, for products labelled organic.

assertions.quote: If it says made with organic ingredients, it needs to be only up to 70% organic.

verdicts.note: 7 CFR 205.301 sets a 70 percent organic minimum for made-with-organic products, which cannot carry the seal.

assertions.quote: Organic farms tend to have better soil health
Organic farms need a lot more space to produce the same amount of food as conventional farms.
On average, organic crop yields are about 20 to 25% lower than conventional ones.
found that organic systems have similar greenhouse emissions to conventional ones, in some cases higher because of the yield factor.
organic foods aren't noticeably more or less nutritious than conventional ones
Antioxidants, though, are a different matter, with some studies showing organic food with 20 to 70% more.
And organic food definitely has less.
